docs.title: KF-Documentation
docs.text: I dump raw stuff into /raw. AI turns it into clean notes in /wiki. That's it.

docs.title: Folders
docs.text:
• /raw — anything I capture: notes, PDFs, screenshots, links
  • /wiki — clean notes written by AI
  • /projects — active work, one folder per project, each with its own README
  • /archive — processed /raw files land here so I can see what's been handled

docs.title: The Loop
docs.text:
1. Write or drop anything into /raw.
  2. Run an AI agent with the prompt in translate.md.
  3. Read the updated /wiki.

The whole folder is a git repo, so nothing is ever lost.

docs.title: Local preview
docs.text:
Install Python and the dependencies in requirements.txt, then run:

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m mkdocs serve

Open the local address shown by MkDocs, normally http://127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: GitHub Pages deployment
docs.text:
The workflow in .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml builds the site on pushes to the master branch and deploys it through GitHub Pages. In the GitHub repository settings, set Pages > Build and deployment > Source to GitHub Actions.

The repository must have a GitHub remote configured before it can be pushed. The workflow publishes the pages listed in mkdocs.yml; raw captures, archive files, prompts, and agent instructions are excluded from the generated site.

docs.title: Purpose and scope
docs.text:
This document describes the Hub Angular GUI down to the relationship between:

  1. application shell and navigation;
  2. lazy-loaded feature areas and screen families;
  3. domain entities and user processes;
  4. forms, validators, guards, resolvers, and HTTP interceptors;
  5. generated API clients, HTTP verbs, URL patterns, request models, and response models; and
  6. screen layout patterns and reusable UI services.

The analysis is based on the Angular source. It describes implemented structure, not necessarily approved business behaviour. The API client under src/app/autogenerated is generated code and should be treated as the canonical endpoint inventory.

docs.title: Bootstrap and shell
docs.text: Layer Source location Responsibility Angular application src/main.ts, src/app/app.component.ts Bootstraps the application and root component. Root module src/app/app.module.ts Registers routing, translation, HTTP, interceptors, Material defaults, notifications, and the authenticated layout. Route table src/app/app-routing.module.ts Redirects the root to dashboard, protects the main shell, and lazy-loads feature modules. Application shell src/app/layout/ Provides the common navigation, page frame, menus, route outlet, and shared layout services. Generated API module src/app/autogenerated/api.module.ts Registers generated domain and integration API services. Configuration src/app/config/, src/app/providers/, src/app.json Loads runtime configuration and administration screens. Shared UI src/app/common/, src/app/shared/, src/app/services/ Reusable controls, dialogs, tables, selectors, attachments, notes, notifications, and utility services.

docs.title: Route and feature map

docs.text:

docs.title: Form and business validation
docs.text:
Feature components use Angular reactive forms (FormBuilder, FormGroup, FormControl, and Validators) for field-level validation. Domain-specific validation is additionally represented by:

  • edit-data and lookup resolvers;
  • generated API command/result types;
  • dedicated validation endpoints, including activity state validation;
  • confirmation modals before destructive or irreversible commands;
  • server error responses surfaced through the shared error interceptor.

The source analysis should distinguish client-side validation from server-side business validation; passing a form does not establish that a domain command will be accepted.

docs.text:

  • KfErrorInterceptor for shared API error handling;

  • ProxyUserInterceptor for proxy-user context;
  • Angular HttpClient with DI interceptors and JSONP support.

docs.title: Generated client contract
docs.text:
Generated services live in src/app/autogenerated/api/. Each service:

  1. injects Angular HttpClient and AppConfigProvider;
  2. creates basePath as ${configProvider.appConfig.rootUrl}/api;
  3. exposes typed methods with generated request interfaces;
  4. serializes query/body/path parameters;
  5. calls a REST endpoint using GET, POST, PUT, or DELETE; and
  6. returns a typed model, query result, command result, or Observable<HttpEvent<T>>.

The effective URL shape is therefore:

{runtime rootUrl}/api/{resource}/{operation}[/{id}][/{sub-resource}]

docs.title: Server-backed rules initiated by the GUI
docs.text:
Before changing an existing Activity or Requirement status, the status control calls the API validation operation. Activity validation includes service line, agency, activity type, CDD state, instructed date, rent data, matching/resale flags, lease completeness, image/brochure presence, and managing department. The API also returns status-specific requirements such as whether a note, completion date, exchanged date, lost-to information, or negotiator restriction applies.

Representative calls are:

POST /api/activities/{id}/stateValidate
POST /api/requirements/{id}/stateValidate

The GUI then opens the required panels, applies client-side form checks, and submits the state/update command. A valid Angular form therefore does not prove that a business transition is valid; the API validation remains authoritative.

docs.title: Scope and goals
docs.text:
The Hub is a business application platform with:

  • an Angular web client;
  • an ASP.NET Web API facade;
  • domain, data-access, and shared infrastructure libraries;
  • SQL Server persistence;
  • asynchronous processing through Azure WebJobs, Azure Storage queues, and Azure Service Bus;
  • document and image storage in Azure Storage;
  • search and indexing through Elasticsearch;
  • integrations with external services such as DocuSign, Fixflo, SLM, Thirdfort, Frontify, email, SAP, and Dotmailer;
  • scheduled, batch, and operational tools;
  • reporting and deployment assets.

The initial documentation scope is Hub only. Azure service-specific documentation should be created later in separate service folders after this baseline has been reviewed.

docs.title: Architecture summary
docs.text:
Hub is best treated as a modular business platform with synchronous and asynchronous execution paths, rather than as a single application:

  1. Users and external clients call the Web API through the Angular application or other API consumers
  2. The API resolves application services through Autofac and uses domain logic, the DAL, SQL Server, search, storage, and external-service adapters
  3. API operations publish work to queues or Service Bus when processing is asynchronous or integration-driven
  4. Azure WebJobs consume queue, Service Bus, and timer-triggered work. They perform notifications, documents, feeds, compliance-related updates, search indexing, messaging, and external integrations
  5. Shared contracts define message subjects and trigger constants so publishers and consumers can interoperate

docs.title: Key architectural characteristics
docs.text:
• Synchronous API path: Angular and other clients call a broad controller surface in the Web API.
  • Shared domain path: API and WebJobs both reference shared domain/common code, so changes to domain behaviour can affect both interactive and background processing.
  • Asynchronous integration: Queue and Service Bus messages decouple API work from long-running, scheduled, or integration-heavy processes.
  • Document-centric storage: Azure Storage abstractions cover blobs, queues, and file shares, including document, image, video, template, and certificate resources.
  • Search projection: Elasticsearch is a separate search/indexing concern and should be documented as a projection of authoritative business data, unless source analysis proves otherwise.
  • Modular background jobs: WebJob projects are feature-oriented, including email, notifications, documents, feeds, SAP, Thirdfort, Elasticsearch, tenancy, and compliance-related processing.
  • Legacy and modern technology coexistence: The repository contains .NET Framework projects and an Angular 19 client, so runtime and deployment compatibility needs explicit documentation.

docs.title: Thirdfort request validation
docs.text:
Source: src/WebJobs/KnightFrank.Antares.WebJobs.Thirdfort/MessageHandlers/ThirdfortRequestQueueMessageHandler.cs.

Feature: Thirdfort request validation

  Scenario: Required-check data is invalid
    Given a Thirdfort request message is received
    When required-check data validation returns errors
    Then the request is not sent to Thirdfort
    And a Thirdfort response message containing those errors is queued

  Scenario: Identity-check data is invalid
    Given a Thirdfort request has valid required-check data
    When identity-check data validation returns errors
    Then the request is not sent to Thirdfort
    And a Thirdfort response message containing those errors is queued

  Scenario: Thirdfort request is accepted
    Given a Thirdfort request passes required-check and identity-check validation
    When the transaction is built and sent successfully
    Then the external transaction identifier is stored against the contact
    And the transaction record is saved

  Scenario: Thirdfort rejects the request
    Given a Thirdfort request passes local validation
    When Thirdfort returns errors
    Then no successful transaction record is stored
    And a Thirdfort response message containing the external errors is queued

docs.title: Thirdfort response processing
docs.text:
Source: src/WebJobs/KnightFrank.Antares.WebJobs.Thirdfort/MessageHandlers/ThirdfortResponseQueueMessageHandler.cs.

Feature: Thirdfort response processing

  Scenario: Thirdfort reports an error
    Given a Thirdfort response is received for an existing contact
    When the response contains one or more errors
    Then the latest contact CDD validity is marked as a Thirdfort error
    And the error description is stored
    And a CDD validity update event is published

  Scenario: Thirdfort report is received
    Given a Thirdfort response is received for an existing contact
    And the response contains no errors
    When the transaction report is downloaded
    Then the report is stored as a CDD PDF blob
    And a current contact attachment is created
    And the external transaction record is deleted
    And the Thirdfort inbox message is acknowledged
    And a CDD validity update event is published

  Scenario: Response references an unknown contact
    Given a Thirdfort response references a contact that cannot be found
    When the response is processed
    Then processing fails explicitly
    And the failure is logged and rethrown for host-level handling

docs.title: Soft opt-in consent lifecycle
docs.text:
Source: src/WebJobs/KnightFrank.Antares.WebJobs.SoftOptIn/CommandHandlers/SoftOptInCommandHandler.cs.

Feature: Soft opt-in consent lifecycle

  Scenario: Contact gains a soft opt-in for a new business entity
    Given a contact is linked to a business for the first time
    When the soft opt-in consent check runs
    Then a soft opt-in consent is created for the contact and business
    And the consent is set to SoftOptin status
    And the consent is assigned an expiry date based on configuration months
    And a SoftOptInYes email notification is sent

  Scenario: Contact loses connection to a business entity
    Given a contact is linked to a business with valid soft opt-in consent
    When the contact is removed from the business
    Then the existing soft opt-in consent may receive a new expiry date
    And audit events record the state transition
    And the contact is removed from affected subscriptions

  Scenario: Existing invalid consent is refreshed
    Given a contact has a consent record for an organisation unit no longer valid
    When the soft opt-in refresh runs
    Then the consent status is set to NotAsked
    And the expiry date is cleared
    And subsequent processing creates a new soft opt-in consent

  Scenario: Contact remains connected to active business
    Given a contact with existing soft opt-in consent is re-validated
    When the contact still has active entities with the business
    Then existing expiry and removal dates are cleared
    And the consent remains valid
    And a SoftOptInContinuation email is sent if renewal is applicable

  Scenario: Soft opt-in consent expires
    Given a contact's soft opt-in consent has an expiry date in the past
    When the consent expiry check runs (processed by renewal handler)
    Then the contact is flagged as requiring consent renewal
    And renewal reminder emails are sent
    (Note: Expiry enforcement is performed by SoftOptInConsentRenewalCommandHandler)

docs.text:
Source: src/WebJobs/KnightFrank.Antares.WebJobs.CddValidity/MessageHandlers/CddValidityRetriggerStatesQueueMessageHandler.cs.

Feature: CDD validity retriggering for related entities

  Scenario: Contact CDD validity changes
    Given a contact's CDD validity state changes
    When a CDD validity retrigger event is received
    Then the system identifies related requirements, instructions, and activities
    And a retrigger event is published for each related entity
    And downstream handlers recalculate CDD validity for those entities

  Scenario: Related requirements are retrieved and retriggered
    Given a contact CDD validity retrigger has been initiated
    When the system looks up related requirements
    Then only active requirements with Applicant party role and non-Unsubmitted CDD status are included
    And a retrigger event is published for each matching requirement

  Scenario: Related instructions are retrieved and retriggered
    Given a contact CDD validity retrigger has been initiated
    When the system looks up related instructions
    Then only active instructions with Client role, non-null CDD completion, and non-excluded status are included
    And a retrigger event is published for each matching instruction

  Scenario: Related activities are retrieved and retriggered
    Given a contact CDD validity retrigger has been initiated
    When the system looks up related activities
    Then only active non-representing activities with Vendor/Landlord role and submitted CDD are included
    And a retrigger event is published for each matching activity

    Given a company's CDD validity state changes
    When a CDD validity retrigger event is received for the company
    Then the system identifies related lease-advisory activities
    And a retrigger event is published for each active lease-advisory activity with submitted CDD
    And downstream handlers recalculate CDD validity for those lease-advisory activities

    Given a CDD validity retrigger event is received

docs.text:
Source: src/WebJobs/KnightFrank.Antares.WebJobs.Notifications/MessageHandlers/PrepareNotificationsQueueMessageHandler.cs and NotificationBlacklistHelper.

Feature: Notification recipient filtering and delivery

  Scenario: User has disabled notifications for a notification type
    Given a notification of type X is to be sent to a user
    When the user has disabled notifications for that notification type
    Then the user is excluded from the recipient list
    And no notification is sent to that user
    And no mobile notification is queued for that user

  Scenario: Notification entity exists and is accessible
    Given a prepare-notifications message is received
    When the entity (activity, requirement, instruction, etc.) must be validated
    Then the system checks that the entity exists
    And the system checks that the user has security access to the entity
    And if either check fails, notification preparation stops with an error

  Scenario: Notification recipient list is generated for secure notification type
    Given a notification is of type ActivityPriceChanged, ActivityStateChanged, or similar secure type
    When recipients are determined
    Then only users with security access to the activity/entity receive the notification
    And additional blacklist filtering is applied

  Scenario: Notification is prepared and queued for delivery
    Given a notification passes all validation and recipient filtering
    When the notification is prepared
    Then a NotificationRecipient record is created for each eligible recipient
    And a BroadcastNotificationsQueueMessage is queued for standard delivery
    And a BroadcastMobileNotificationsQueueMessage is queued for mobile-push delivery
    And a suitable notification title is generated based on the notification type

docs.title: Tenancy lifecycle integration rules
docs.text:
Source: tenancy SLM, Fixflo, churn-risk, and out-of-hours handlers.

Feature: Tenancy lifecycle integrations

  Scenario: SLM sync only processes parties without a Qube person ID
    Given a tenancy SLM message is received
    When the tenancy has tenant or landlord parties without a Qube person ID
    Then the system retrieves people from SLM using the tenancy SLM reference
    And matching party records receive their Qube person IDs
    And unmatched parties create Qube person-record exceptions

  Scenario: SLM API failure is recorded as a tenancy exception
    Given a tenancy SLM message is received
    When the SLM response is unsuccessful
    Then a tenancy Qube API exception is stored
    And the party records are not updated from the failed response

  Scenario: Fixflo start events only include eligible tenancies
    Given the Fixflo tenancy-start job runs
    When a tenancy is managed, residential, located in the UK, and has started without expiring
    And it has an allowed party that has not been sent to Fixflo
    Then a Fixflo tenancy-started event is published
    And successfully published parties are marked as sent to Fixflo

  Scenario: Churn-risk updates create an audit trail
    Given a tenancy churn-risk update is received
    When the new churn-risk differs from the stored value
    Then the tenancy is saved
    And the change is audited
    And a tenancy note is created
    And the tenancy search projection is refreshed

  Scenario: Out-of-hours archival requires an old expired tenancy with no replacement
    Given the out-of-hours archival job runs
    When a managed ILM tenancy expired more than six months ago
    And it is not fallen through, already removed, or excluded by department
    And its activity has no current managed replacement tenancy
    Then the tenancy is marked as automatically removed from the out-of-hours list
    And the change is audited

docs.title: Brochure generation rules
docs.text:
Source: src/WebJobs/KnightFrank.Antares.WebJobs/MessageHandlers/GenerateBrochureQueueMessageHandler.cs and CompleteBrochuresQueueMessageHandler.cs.

Feature: Brochure generation

  Scenario: A brochure without a template uses all available brochure items
    Given a brochure request has no template name
    When brochure data is built for the activity
    Then all available brochure items are included
    And the request is marked as custom
    And no template ID is sent

  Scenario: A named brochure template must exist in Frontify
    Given a brochure request has a template name
    When Frontify returns no matching template
    Then brochure generation fails with a template-not-found error
    And no Frontify generation event is published

  Scenario: Brochure completion is only sent for residential sales or lettings
    Given a brochure completion message is received for an existing activity
    When the activity service line is residential sales or residential lettings
    Then a Frontify completion request is sent using the activity ID
    Otherwise no Frontify completion request is sent

docs.title: Integration result rules
docs.text:
Source: HomePplResultQueueMessageHandler.cs, TDSResultQueueMessageHandler.cs, and QubeSynchronizationQueueMessageHandler.cs.

Feature: Integration result processing

  Scenario: HomePpl reference reports are attached to the relevant party
    Given a HomePpl reference-check result contains a risk-report blob
    When the tenancy and party exist
    Then the report is stored in Blob Storage
    And the report is attached to the permitted occupier, tenant, or guarantor
    And the reference-check status is set to received
    And a tenancy progression update event is published

  Scenario: TDS success stores and synchronizes a certificate
    Given a successful TDS result contains a certificate URL
    When the certificate download succeeds
    Then the deposit status is set to registered
    And the certificate metadata and attachment are saved
    And Qube synchronization is queued for the tenancy and its attachments

  Scenario: TDS failure stores returned errors
    Given a TDS result is unsuccessful
    When the result contains errors
    Then the deposit status is set to not registered
    And the serialized errors are stored
    And a deposit-registration-failed event is published

  Scenario: Stale Qube synchronization messages are skipped
    Given a Qube synchronization message is received
    When a newer successful synchronization already exists
    Then the message is logged as stale
    And no entity is sent to Qube

  Scenario: Unsupported Qube entity types are rejected
    Given a Qube synchronization message has an unsupported entity type
    When the handler validates the message
    Then processing fails with an out-of-range error
    And the failure is logged and rethrown

docs.title: Email consent and suppression rules
docs.text:
Source: Dotmailer email handlers, suppression runners, and SendEmailQueueMessageHandler.

Feature: Email consent and suppression

  Scenario: Consent-specific Dotmailer email is revalidated before sending
    Given a Dotmailer email is queued for a contact and business
    When the contact email and contact still exist
    Then the handler resolves the business-specific consent
    And the email is sent only if the email type's consent condition is still true

  Scenario: Email for a deleted contact is skipped
    Given a Dotmailer email is queued for a contact
    When the contact no longer exists
    Then the email is not sent

  Scenario: Incremental Dotmailer suppression import creates local records
    Given the Dotmailer suppression job is enabled
    When a suppressed contact is returned since the last run
    Then a suppression record is stored for that email and business
    And a local suppression command is sent for the new suppression

  Scenario: Dotmailer resubscription removes local suppression
    Given a contact has a local Dotmailer suppression for a business
    When Dotmailer reports the contact as modified during a later run
    Then the matching suppression record is removed for that business

  Scenario: Email with no allowed recipients is handled without sending
    Given an outbox email has recipients
    When the allowed-address whitelist removes every recipient
    Then the email is treated as successfully handled
    And no message is sent

  Scenario: Email send failures retry up to the configured handler limit
    Given an outbox or error email is being sent
    When the email strategy throws an exception
    Then the send retry count is incremented
    And the error details are stored
    And the email is marked Error after five or more retries

docs.title: Production naming convention
docs.text:
The physical Azure entity names follow the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) naming convention. In practice, the production form retains the entity, workload, region, and instance components and changes only the environment component from local or dev to prd where that component is present. For example, a sbt-activity-local-ee value would become sbt-activity-prd-ee, subject to the deployment template's exact token placement.

Production validation should therefore confirm:

  • the deployment parameters or environment settings that replace the local/dev environment token with prd;
  • that the entity, workload, region, and instance components remain unchanged;
  • that the injected names match the infrastructure definitions and CAF naming convention; and
  • whether any service-specific abbreviations or legacy exceptions are approved.

The checked-in local-ee and dev-ne values above are dev/local names only and must not be presented as production names.

docs.title: Processing pattern
docs.text:
1. A controller, domain service, timer, webhook, or integration publishes a message
  2. Azure Storage Queue or Service Bus delivers the message to the WebJobs host
  3. A feature module resolves a handler through the dependency-injection container
  4. The handler validates and processes the message
  5. The handler writes to SQL, Blob Storage, Elasticsearch, or an external service
  6. Failures are logged and rethrown in the inspected Thirdfort handlers, allowing the host's configured retry behaviour to apply

docs.title: Hub API Workflows - Main User Journeys and Integration Points
Overview
docs.text: This document maps the main user workflows through the Hub API endpoints, showing how contacts, properties, activities, requirements, and tenancies interact. Each workflow illustrates a complete business process from start to finish.

docs.title: Workflow 1: Create and Market a Property (Lettings)
docs.text:
Scenario: Landlord wants to let their office building

Actors: Landlord Contact, Negotiator (assigned agent), Property, Activity (lettings instruction), Requirement (tenant looking), Tenancy

docs.title: API Sequence
docs.text:
1. Create Property
   POST /properties
   {
     address: "123 Business Street, London",
     propertyType: "Office",
     division: "Commercial",
     characteristics: { totalArea: 10000, floors: 3, features: [...] }
   }
   → Property ID: prop-001

2. Add Ownership
   POST /properties/prop-001/ownerships
   {
     ownerContactId: contact-landlord-001,
     percentage: 100,
     managingCompanyId: company-001
   }

3. Create Lettings Activity (Marketing Instruction)
   POST /activities
   {
     propertyId: prop-001,
     activityType: "Lettings",
     activitySubType: "New Let",
     serviceLine: "Commercial Lettings",
     parties: [
       { role: "Landlord", contactId: contact-landlord-001 },
       { role: "Agent", contactId: contact-agent-001, negotiatorId: negotiator-001 }
     ],
     status: "Live"
   }
   → Activity ID: act-001

4. Set Marketing Details
   PUT /activities/act-001
   {
     marketedDate: "2026-11-17",
     agencyExpiry: "2027-05-17",
     quotedRent: 50000,  // annual
     marketingImages: [image1.jpg, image2.jpg, ...],
     description: "Modern office space, flexible lease..."
   }

5. Publish to Fixflo (Marketing Platform)
   POST /activities/act-001/marketing/fixflo
   {
     fixtloReference: "FXF-12345",
     publishDate: "2026-11-17",
     listingStatus: "Active"
   }
   → Marketing begins, reaches prospective tenants

6. [Matching begins asynchronously]
   System finds Requirement records matching criteria
   (Location: London, Space: 8000-15000 sqm, Rent: £40-60k annual)

7. Tenant creates Requirement (separately, by their own API call)
   POST /requirements
   {
     requirementType: "Tenant Requirement",
     applicantContactId: contact-tenant-001,
     criteria: {
       propertyTypes: ["Office"],
       priceRange: { min: 40000, max: 60000 },
       sizeRange: { min: 8000, max: 15000 },
       location: "London",
       tenantType: "Corporate"
     },
     status: "Active"
   }
   → Requirement ID: req-001

8. Auto-Match (scheduler runs nightly or on-demand)
   System matches req-001 to act-001 (property meets criteria)

9. Requirement matches Activity
   POST /requirements/req-001/matches/act-001
   {
     matchScore: 0.95,  // 95% match
     reasonForMatch: "Size, rent, location all match tenant criteria"
   }
   → Match ID: match-001

10. Tenant views matched properties and schedules viewing
    POST /requirements/req-001/viewings
    {
      activityId: act-001,
      preferredDate: "2026-11-25",
      preferredTime: "14:00"
    }
    → Viewing ID: view-001
    → Negotiator notified

11. Viewing happens, tenant interested, makes Offer
    POST /activities/act-001/offers
    {
      offerorContactId: contact-tenant-001,
      offeredRent: 45000,
      proposedCommencement: "2027-01-15",
      proposedLease: 3,  // 3-year lease
      leaseTerm: { breaks: [], reviews: ["Annually"] }
    }
    → Offer ID: offer-001

12. Landlord accepts Offer
    PUT /offers/offer-001
    {
      status: "Accepted",
      acceptedDate: "2026-11-26",
      acceptedRent: 45000
    }

13. Activity moves to "Under Offer"
    PUT /activities/act-001/status
    {
      status: "Under Offer",
      statusReason: "Offer accepted from tenant-contact-001",
      acceptedOfferRent: 45000,
      agreedCommencement: "2027-01-15"
    }

14. Activity moves to Completion
    PUT /activities/act-001/status
    {
      status: "Completed",
      completionDate: "2026-12-20",
      completionReason: "Lease exchange and completion"
    }

15. Create Tenancy (from Activity)
    POST /tenancies
    {
      propertyId: prop-001,
      activityId: act-001,  // Link back to activity
      requirementId: req-001,  // Link to requirement
      tenancyType: "Full Repairing",
      parties: [
        { role: "Tenant", contactId: contact-tenant-001 },
        { role: "Landlord", contactId: contact-landlord-001 }
      ],
      terms: {
        completionDate: "2026-12-20",
        commencementDate: "2027-01-15",
        expiryDate: "2030-01-14",  // 3-year term
        rentPerAnnum: 45000,
        rentPayment: "Quarterly in advance",
        leaseBreak: null  // No break clause
      },
      status: "Draft"
    }
    → Tenancy ID: ten-001

16. Right-to-Rent Check
    POST /tenancies/ten-001/right-to-rent
    {
      checkDate: "2026-12-15",
      companyRegistration: "12345678",
      directorVerified: true,
      documentationType: "Certificate of Incorporation"
    }
    → Status: "Verified"

17. Activate Tenancy (move to live/active status)
    PUT /tenancies/ten-001/activate
    {
      activationDate: "2027-01-15",
      rentsCollectionMethod: "Direct Debit",
      managingAgent: negotiator-001
    }
    → Tenancy now LIVE, rent tracking begins

18. [Later: Renewal tracking begins]
    As expiry date approaches (2030-01-14), system flags for renewal
    New Renewal record created for decision (renew, let expire, or renegotiate)

Outcome: Property successfully let, tenancy created and activated, rent tracking begins

docs.title: Workflow 2: Buy/Sell Activity with Chain Transaction
docs.text: Scenario: Investor buying office building; seller must buy another property first (chain)

docs.title: API Sequence
docs.text:
1. Seller creates Activity (Sales Instruction)
   POST /activities
   {
     propertyId: prop-002,
     activityType: "Sales",
     activitySubType: "Investment Property",
     serviceLine: "Commercial Sales",
     parties: [
       { role: "Vendor", contactId: contact-seller-001 },
       { role: "Agent", contactId: contact-agent-001 }
     ],
     status: "Live"
   }
   → Activity ID: act-seller-001

2. Buyer creates Requirement
   POST /requirements
   {
     requirementType: "Buyer Requirement",
     applicantContactId: contact-buyer-001,
     criteria: {
       propertyTypes: ["Office"],
       priceRange: { min: 500000, max: 750000 },
       location: "London",
       sector: "Commercial",
       investmentYield: 4.5  // Looking for 4.5%+ yield
     }
   }
   → Requirement ID: req-buyer-001

3. Requirement matched to Activity
   POST /requirements/req-buyer-001/matches/act-seller-001
   {
     matchScore: 0.92
   }
   → Match ID: match-buyer-001

4. Buyer's Offer
   POST /activities/act-seller-001/offers
   {
     offerorContactId: contact-buyer-001,
     offeredPrice: 650000,
     exchangeDate: "2027-02-15",
     completionDate: "2027-03-15",
     conditions: ["Subject to satisfactory survey", "Subject to finance"]
   }
   → Offer ID: offer-buyer-001

5. Seller Accepts (but seller must also buy another property first - chain)

   Seller creates their own Requirement (looking to buy replacement property)
   POST /requirements
   {
     requirementType: "Seller/Buyer Requirement",
     applicantContactId: contact-seller-001,
     criteria: { /* replacement property criteria */ }
   }
   → Requirement ID: req-seller-buying-001

6. Seller finds matching replacement property
   Activity for replacement property is found/created
   POST /activities
   {
     propertyId: prop-replacement-001,
     activityType: "Purchase",  // Seller is now buying
     parties: [
       { role: "Buyer", contactId: contact-seller-001 },  // Seller acting as buyer
       { role: "Vendor", contactId: contact-replacement-seller-001 }
     ]
   }
   → Activity ID: act-replacement-001

7. Create Chain Transaction linking both activities
   POST /activities/act-seller-001/chain-transactions
   {
     linkedActivityId: act-replacement-001,
     chainPosition: 1,  // Position in chain
     chainDependency: "MUST_COMPLETE_REPLACEMENT_FIRST",
     chainNotes: "Seller must complete purchase of replacement before selling current property"
   }

8. Chain activities progress together:
   - act-replacement-001 → Exchange → Completion (seller buys replacement)
   - act-seller-001 → Exchange → Completion (seller's original property sold to buyer)

9. Final completion of original sale
   PUT /activities/act-seller-001/status
   {
     status: "Completed",
     completionDate: "2027-03-15",
     completionPrice: 650000,
     exchangeDate: "2027-02-15",
     chainCompletionSequence: 1  // Completed first in chain
   }

10. Buyer becomes Owner
    POST /properties/prop-002/ownerships
    {
      ownerContactId: contact-buyer-001,
      percentage: 100,
      acquisitionDate: "2027-03-15",
      acquisitionPrice: 650000
    }

Outcome: Chain transaction successfully completed, buyer now owns property, seller has completed purchase of replacement property

docs.title: Workflow 3: Requirement Auto-Matching and Viewing Tour
docs.text: Scenario: Tenant has active requirement; scheduled matcher finds and notifies of matches

docs.title: API Sequence
docs.text:

6. Viewings occur, tenant feedback recorded

7. Negotiator creates offers for interested properties

docs.title: Workflow 4: Tenancy Renewal and Extension
docs.text: Scenario: Tenancy expiry approaching; landlord and tenant need to agree renewal terms

docs.title: API Sequence
docs.text:
1. Tenancy reaching expiry (e.g., 6 months before end date)
   System flags tenancy for renewal workflow
   GET /tenancies/ten-002
   → Expiry date: "2027-01-15" (6 months away)

2. Negotiator initiates renewal process
   POST /tenancies/ten-002/renewal
   {
     renewalOptionDate: "2026-07-15",  // Decision date
     proposedRenewalTerms: {
       newExpiryDate: "2030-01-15",  // Another 3 years
       proposedRent: 46000,  // 2.2% increase
       rentReviewFrequency: "Annual",
       proposedBreaks: [{ breakDate: "2028-01-15" }]
     },
     renewalNotes: "2.2% increase in line with inflation; tenant-friendly break at 2 years"
   }
   → Renewal ID: renew-001

3. Landlord reviews and approves renewal terms
   PUT /tenancies/ten-002/renewal/renew-001
   {
     status: "Approved",
     approvedDate: "2026-06-30",
     approvedRent: 46000,
     approvedExpiryDate: "2030-01-15",
     approvedBreaks: [{ breakDate: "2028-01-15" }],
     landlordNotes: "Tenant has been reliable; happy with renewal terms"
   }

4. Tenant notified of renewal terms
   Send notification via API (tenant receives via portal/email)

5. Tenant accepts renewal
   PUT /tenancies/ten-002/renewal/renew-001
   {
     tenantAcceptance: "Accepted",
     tenantAcceptanceDate: "2026-07-01",
     tenantNotes: "Break clause at year 2 is important for us"
   }

6. Create new Tenancy record for renewal period
   POST /tenancies
   {
     propertyId: prop-001,
     previousTenancyId: ten-002,  // Link to prior tenancy
     parties: [ /* same as previous */ ],
     terms: {
       commencementDate: "2027-01-15",  // Start of renewal period
       expiryDate: "2030-01-15",
       rentPerAnnum: 46000,
       breaks: [{ breakDate: "2028-01-15" }]
     },
     status: "Draft"
   }
   → New Tenancy ID: ten-003

7. Activate new tenancy at commencement
   PUT /tenancies/ten-003/activate
   {
     activationDate: "2027-01-15"
   }

8. Update rent collection configuration
   PUT /tenancies/ten-003
   {
     rentAmount: 46000,
     rentPaymentMethod: "Direct Debit",
     rentPaymentFrequency: "Quarterly in advance"
   }

9. If tenant doesn't accept renewal:
   PUT /tenancies/ten-002/status
   {
     status: "Expired",
     expiryDate: "2027-01-15",
     renewalOutcome: "Tenant vacated; not renewed"
   }
   → End of tenancy workflow

Outcome: Tenancy renewed with agreed terms, new tenancy record created, or tenancy ended if not renewed

docs.title: Workflow 5: Property with Multiple Tenancies
docs.text: Scenario: Multi-let building with 10 tenancies across different units, various renewal dates

docs.title: API Sequence
docs.text:
1. Property structure
   Property: prop-multilet-001 (whole building)
     ├─ Unit 1 (1000 sqm): Tenancy ten-m1 (expires 2027-03-15)
     ├─ Unit 2 (1200 sqm): Tenancy ten-m2 (expires 2028-06-30)

3. Identify tenancies requiring attention (expiring within 6 months)

4. For ten-m3 (expiring soon: 2026-12-01)

   {
     renewalOptionDate: "2026-10-01",
     proposedRenewalTerms: { /* ... */ }
   }

5. If tenant vacates at end of date:
   PUT /tenancies/ten-m3/status
   {
     status: "Expired",
     expiryDate: "2026-12-01",
     vacationDate: "2026-12-01",
     unitAvailability: "Available for new let"
   }

6. Create new Activity for re-let (Unit 3)

7. New tenancy created when new tenant found

     parties: [ /* new tenant */ ],

   }

8. Negotiator tracks property occupancy
   GET /properties/prop-multilet-001/occupancy
   → Returns: 90% occupied (9 of 10 units let)
   → Vacant units: ["Unit 3 (re-letting in progress)"]

Outcome: Property portfolio management, multi-tenancy tracking, coordinated renewals and re-letting

docs.title: Workflow 6: CDD Compliance and Right-to-Rent Checks
docs.text: Scenario: Activity and tenancy require compliance verification before completion

docs.title: API Sequence
docs.text:
1. Activity/Tenancy created with parties
   Must verify CDD (Customer Due Diligence) before completion

2. For Activity with vendor requiring CDD:
   POST /activities/act-001/cdd
   {
     vendorContactId: contact-seller-001,
     complianceRequirement: "Full CDD - Investment property sale >£500k",
     documentationRequired: ["Proof of identity", "Proof of address", "Corporate structure"]
   }
   → CDD ID: cdd-001

3. CDD handler (Thirdfort integration) processes verification
   POST /cdd-handler/process
   {
     cddId: cdd-001,
     partyContactId: contact-seller-001,
     partyType: "Company"
   }
   → Sends to Thirdfort for verification

4. Thirdfort returns verification results
   - If verified: CDD status = "Completed", Activity can proceed
   - If warnings: CDD status = "Warning - Review Required"
   - If failed: CDD status = "Failed - Cannot proceed"

5. For Tenancy with right-to-rent check (before commencement):
   POST /tenancies/ten-001/right-to-rent
   {
     partyContactId: contact-tenant-001,
     partyType: "Company",
     documentationType: "Certificate of Incorporation",
     documentationDate: "2026-10-01",
     directorName: "John Doe"
   }
   → RTR check sent to external service (e.g., Qube)

6. Right-to-rent verification returns
   - If verified: RTR status = "Verified", Tenancy can commence
   - If failed: RTR status = "Failed - Cannot commence"

7. Activity/Tenancy CDD/RTR gates completion/commencement
   PUT /activities/act-001/status
   {
     status: "Completion",
     completionDate: "2027-03-15",
     cddVerified: true,  // Must be true to allow completion
     cddCompletionDate: "2027-02-20"
   }

   PUT /tenancies/ten-001/activate
   {
     activationDate: "2027-01-15",
     rightToRentVerified: true,  // Must be true to allow commencement
     rightToRentVerificationDate: "2026-12-20"
   }

Outcome: Compliance verified before activity completion and tenancy commencement

docs.title: Hub Core Domain - Contact, Property, Activity, and Requirement Management
Overview
docs.text:
The Hub is a relationship and transaction management platform for commercial real estate. It tracks:

  • Contacts — buyers, sellers, tenants, landlords, agents, professionals
  • Properties — office, industrial, retail assets with ownerships and tenancies
  • Activities — marketing instructions, transactions, negotiations on properties
  • Requirements — what buyers/sellers/tenants/landlords are looking for
  • Tenancies — landlord-tenant relationships with compliance, rent management, and renewal

docs.title: Process 1: Contact and Relationship Management
docs.text:
Actors: Contact, Negotiator (assigned staff), Company, Properties, Requirements

Flow:

  1. Contact record created (buyer, seller, tenant, landlord, agent, professional)
  2. Contact details added (address, phone, email, company, negotiator assignment)
  3. Contact interests captured (property types, locations, transaction types)
  4. Consents managed (marketing, newsletters, soft opt-in, CDD compliance)
  5. Contact linked to requirements (what they're looking for)
  6. Contact linked to activities (properties they're viewing/transacting on)
  7. Contact linked to ownerships (properties they own)
  8. Contact linked to tenancies (properties they occupy)
  9. Contact relationships tracked (clients they've introduced, referral chains)

Key Business Rules:

  • Contact must have primary negotiator assigned
  • Contact consents must be validated (soft opt-in, CDD, marketing)
  • Prospect contacts may become active, deceased, retired, or locked
  • Contact name/address changes are audited
  • Multiple contact records may be identified as duplicates and merged

Data Model:

  • Contact (Id, Names, Salutation, Nationality, Profession, BirthDate)
  • ContactAddress (Primary, Business, Correspondence, Delivery)
  • ContactPhone, ContactEmail, ContactSocial
  • ContactCompany (Employment, Ownership)
  • ContactNegotiator (Assigned staff)
  • ContactType, ContactInterest, Consent, SoftOptin

Key APIs:

  • POST /contacts — Create contact
  • PUT /contacts/{id} — Update contact details
  • PUT /contacts/{id}/negotiator — Assign negotiator
  • POST /contacts/{id}/addresses — Add address
  • PUT /contacts/{id}/consents — Update marketing/CDD consents
  • POST /contacts/merge — Merge duplicate contacts
  • GET /contacts/search — Find contacts by criteria

docs.title: Process 2: Property and Ownership Management
docs.text:
Actors: Property, Owner Contact/Company, Negotiator, Property Manager

Flow:

  1. Property created with address, type, division, characteristics
  2. Ownership added (contact/company, percentage, management details)
  3. Property characteristics documented (floors, areas, WAULT, amenities)
  4. Property marketed through Activities
  5. Tenancies created on property
  6. Property may be archived or deleted (soft delete with versioning)

Key Business Rules:

  • Property must have address and type
  • Property may have multiple owners (fractional ownership)
  • Property manager assigned for management activities
  • Property characteristics (area, floors) must be valid
  • Property may be linked to development/estate/phase
  • Duplicate properties can be merged

Data Model:

  • Property (Id, Address, PropertyType, Division, Phase, Estate)
  • PropertyCharacteristics (TotalArea, Floors, WAULT, Acreage)
  • Ownership (Property, Owner Contact/Company, Percentage, Manager)
  • PropertyContact (Property Manager, Maintenance Contact, etc.)

Key APIs:

  • POST /properties — Create property
  • PUT /properties/{id} — Update property details
  • POST /properties/{id}/ownerships — Add ownership
  • PUT /properties/{id}/ownerships/{oid} — Update ownership
  • POST /properties/{id}/areas — Document floor/area details
  • PUT /properties/{id}/merge — Merge duplicate property
  • GET /properties/search — Find properties

docs.title: Process 3: Activity (Marketing Instruction) Lifecycle
docs.text:
Actors: Property, Negotiator, Activity Parties (Vendor, Landlord, Agent, Tenant, Buyer), Requirements, Offers

Flow:

  1. Activity created on property (instruction to market or manage)
  2. Activity type, sub-type, and service-line defined (sales, lettings, management, acquisition)
  3. Parties added (vendors, landlords, agents, negotiators, solicitors)
  4. Marketing started (Fixflo listing, brochures, images, advertising)
  5. Viewings/Appointments scheduled
  6. Requirements matched to activity (qualified leads)
  7. Offers received (from interested parties)
  8. Offer accepted (transaction progresses)
  9. Activity moves to completion (tenancy created) or withdrawn

Key Business Rules:

  • Activity must reference a property
  • Activity type determines allowed parties and workflows
  • Activity status controls allowed operations (can't accept offer if withdrawn)
  • Status changes are timestamped and audited
  • Price changes must be recorded (quoted vs. agreed)
  • Chain transactions link multiple activities (dependent transactions)
  • Withdrawal must include reason (sold elsewhere, deceased, etc.)
  • Marketing expiry dates control advertising lifecycle
  • CDD/Appraisal records must be maintained for compliance

Activity Status State Machine:

  • Live → Active marketing, accepting viewings, receiving offers
  • Under Offer → Accepted offer, awaiting completion
  • Completion → Transaction completed, tenancy or ownership transferred
  • Withdrawn → Marketing stopped, reason recorded

Data Model:

  • Activity (Id, PropertyId, ActivityTypeId, ActivitySubTypeId, ActivityStatusId)
  • ActivityParty (Activity, PartyRole: Vendor/Landlord/Agent/Buyer/Tenant/Introducer/Solicitor)
  • ActivityPrice (Quoted, Agreed, Rent values)
  • ActivityMarketing (Fixflo, Images, Advertisements, Marketing Expiry)
  • ActivityOffer (Accepted/Rejected, Offeror)
  • ActivityMatch (Linked Requirement, Why matched)
  • ActivityChainTransaction (Linked Activity, Dependency)

Key APIs:

  • POST /activities — Create activity (instruction)
  • PUT /activities/{id} — Update activity details
  • POST /activities/{id}/parties — Add party (vendor, agent, etc.)
  • PUT /activities/{id}/price — Update price/rent
  • POST /activities/{id}/offers — Receive offer
  • POST /activities/{id}/matches — Match requirement to activity
  • PUT /activities/{id}/status — Change status (live → under-offer → completion)
  • POST /activities/{id}/marketing/fixflo — Publish to Fixflo
  • POST /activities/{id}/brochure — Generate brochure
  • POST /activities/{id}/complete — Mark as completed (tenancy created)
  • GET /activities/search — Find activities by property, negotiator, status

docs.title: Process 4: Requirement and Matching
docs.text:
Actors: Requirement (Tenant/Buyer/Seller), Applicant Contact, Activities, Matches, Viewings, Offers

Flow:

  1. Requirement created (contact looking to buy, let space, or sell property)
  2. Requirement type defined (tenant requirement, buyer requirement, seller instruction)
  3. Criteria captured (price/rent range, location, size, tenure, tenant type, features)
  4. Requirement assigned to negotiator
  5. Automated matching algorithm finds activities matching criteria
  6. Requirement matched to activities (qualified opportunities)
  7. Viewings arranged for matched activities
  8. Offers made to applicant
  9. Requirement progresses to completion (tenancy/sale) or withdrawn

Key Business Rules:

  • Requirement must have applicant contact
  • Requirement criteria must be valid (price/rent ranges, dates, etc.)
  • Requirement status controls allowed operations
  • Requirements can be auto-matched (scheduled matching runs)
  • Requirement hotness score reflects activity level
  • Selling status and next-action guide workflow (for seller requirements)
  • CDD status tracked separately from requirement status
  • Requirement may link to current/selling property (what they currently occupy/own)

Requirement Status State Machine:

  • Active → Seeking properties, reviewing matches, arranging viewings
  • Matched → Found property, offer pending or accepted
  • Sold/Completed → Transaction completed
  • Withdrawn → No longer seeking

Data Model:

  • Requirement (Id, RequirementTypeId, RequirementStatusId, ApplicantContactId)
  • RequirementParty (Requirement, PartyRole, Contact)
  • RequirementCriteria (PropertyTypes, PriceRange, RentRange, LocationPreferences)
  • RequirementMatch (Requirement, Activity, MatchScore, Status)
  • RequirementOffer (Requirement, Activity, OfferTerms, Status)
  • RequirementViewing (Requirement, Activity, AppointmentDate)

Key APIs:

  • POST /requirements — Create requirement (tenant/buyer/seller looking for property)
  • PUT /requirements/{id} — Update requirement criteria
  • POST /requirements/{id}/parties — Add party (co-applicant, etc.)
  • GET /requirements/{id}/matches — Find matching activities
  • POST /requirements/{id}/matches/{aid} — Accept/create match
  • POST /requirements/{id}/offers — Generate offer to applicant
  • POST /requirements/{id}/viewings — Schedule viewing
  • PUT /requirements/{id}/status — Progress requirement (active → matched → completed)
  • GET /requirements/search — Find requirements by criteria

docs.title: Process 5: Tenancy and Property Management
docs.text:
Actors: Tenancy (Landlord, Tenant, Guarantor), Property, Related Activity, Linked Requirement, Negotiator

Flow:

  1. Tenancy created (from activity match or manual creation)
  2. Parties assigned (tenant, landlord, guarantor, management company)
  3. Lease terms documented (commencement, expiry, rent, fees, breaks)
  4. Completion recorded
  5. Commencement date — tenancy becomes active
  6. Right-to-rent checks performed (UK compliance)
  7. Guarantor checks and verification
  8. Rent reviews and reviews occur
  9. Break clauses exercised (optional early exit)
  10. Renewal records tracked
  11. Expiry date approaches — renewal or surrender option
  12. Tenancy surrendered (early or at end date) or renewed

Key Business Rules:

  • Tenancy must reference property and have parties (tenant, landlord)
  • Commencement date must be after completion date
  • Expiry date must be after commencement date
  • Rent/fees must be positive
  • Right-to-rent status must be verified before commencement (compliance)
  • Guarantor verification required (if guarantor present)
  • Tenancy progression through stages (activation → completion → commencement)
  • Renewal options and terms documented
  • Linked Activity records what activity created this tenancy
  • Linked Requirement records what requirement was matched
  • Soft-delete and versioning for audit
  • Churn-risk calculated (likelihood tenant will leave)

Tenancy Lifecycle State Machine:

  • Draft → Created but not yet active/completed
  • Active (Live) → Commenced, rent-paying
  • Completed → Transaction closed
  • Expired → End date passed, no renewal
  • Surrendered → Early termination, tenant departed
  • Renewed → Links to next tenancy record

Data Model:

  • Tenancy (Id, AssetId, TenancyTypeId, TenancyStatusId)
  • TenancyParty (Tenancy, PartyRole: Tenant/Landlord/Guarantor/Agent)
  • TenancyTerms (CommencementDate, ExpiryDate, SurrenderDate, RentAmount)
  • TenancyBreak (BreakDate, ExercisedDate, Status)
  • TenancyRenewal (OptionDate, RenewalTerms, ApprovedDate)
  • RightToRent (Status, ExpirationDate, DocumentationDate)
  • TenancyProgression (ActivationDate, CompletionDate, Checks: Guarantor, Insurance, etc.)
  • TenancyLinkedActivity (Related Activity that produced this tenancy)
  • TenancyLinkedRequirement (Related Requirement that was matched)

Key APIs:

  • POST /tenancies — Create tenancy (from activity or manual)
  • PUT /tenancies/{id} — Update tenancy terms
  • POST /tenancies/{id}/parties — Add party (tenant, landlord, guarantor)
  • PUT /tenancies/{id}/activate — Activate tenancy (move to live)
  • PUT /tenancies/{id}/end-date — Update end date (break exercise, renewal extension)
  • PUT /tenancies/{id}/terminate — Surrender tenancy early
  • POST /tenancies/{id}/right-to-rent — Record right-to-rent check
  • POST /tenancies/{id}/progression-checks — Guarantor verification, insurance, etc.
  • POST /tenancies/{id}/renewal — Create renewal record
  • GET /tenancies/search — Find tenancies by property, tenant, status
  • PUT /tenancies/{id}/status — Manage lifecycle (active → completed → expired/renewed)

docs.title: Journey 1: Tenant Looking for Office Space
docs.text:
1. Tenant Contact submits Requirement (100 sq m office, £5k/month, West London)
  2. System auto-matches Requirement to current Activities on the market
  3. Matching Activities shown to negotiator (properties meeting criteria)
  4. Viewings scheduled for top matches
  5. Tenant likes one property → Offer made
  6. Landlord accepts offer (Activity moves to "Under Offer" → "Completion")
  7. Tenancy created with matching terms (commencement, rent, parties)
  8. Right-to-rent check performed
  9. Tenancy becomes live on commencement date
  10. Rent tracked, renewal options monitored

docs.title: Journey 2: Property Owner Selling a Building
docs.text:
1. Property listed in system (address, type, ownership)
  2. Owner creates Activity (sales instruction)
  3. Marketing setup (brochure, Fixflo listing, images)
  4. Potential buyers create Requirements (what they're looking for)
  5. System matches Requirements to this Activity
  6. Viewings scheduled
  7. Buyer makes an Offer
  8. Activity moves to "Under Offer"
  9. If accepted → completion and Activity finalized
  10. If ownership changes → Ownership record updated
  11. Building may be leased → new Tenancies on the property

docs.title: Journey 3: Agent Managing Multiple Properties
docs.text:
1. Agent assigned as Negotiator for property portfolio
  2. Agent creates/manages Activities (marketing instructions, tenancy management)
  3. Agent reviews incoming Requirement matches
  4. Agent schedules Viewings/Appointments with interested parties
  5. Agent negotiates Offers
  6. Agent manages Tenancies (renewals, right-to-rent, compliance checks)
  7. Agent coordinates with Parties (vendors, landlords, tenants, solicitors)
  8. Agent prepares brochures, marketing images, documentation

docs.title: Contact Rules
docs.text:
• Contact must have at least one negotiator assignment
  • Contact consents must be managed (CDD, marketing, newsletters)
  • Soft opt-in consent expires after configured period
  • Contact may be marked deceased or retired (soft deletion)
  • Duplicate contacts can be merged (manual process)
  • Contact relationships to companies, properties, requirements must be maintained

docs.title: Activity Rules
docs.text:
• Activity must reference valid property
  • Activity type must match property type (can't rent out a sale-only property)
  • Party roles must be valid for activity type (vendor required for sales, landlord for lettings)
  • Activity status changes are timestamped and must follow allowed transitions
  • Withdrawal reason is mandatory
  • Price changes create audit trail (quoted vs. agreed)
  • Chain transactions link dependent activities (can't complete A without completing B first)
  • CDD/Appraisal records are compliance requirements
  • Marketing expiry controls Fixflo/advertising lifecycle

docs.title: Requirement Rules
docs.text:
• Requirement must have applicant contact
  • Requirement criteria must be internally consistent (price range: min ≤ max)
  • Requirement status controls allowed changes (can't match if completed/withdrawn)
  • Auto-matching runs on schedule (nightly or on-demand)
  • Requirements link to current property (what applicant currently owns/occupies)
  • CDD status tracked separately (may be in progress, completed, warning)
  • Hotness score affects priority in matching

docs.title: Tenancy Rules
docs.text:
• Tenancy must reference property and have required parties
  • Commencement date must be after completion/agreement date
  • Expiry date must be after commencement date
  • Rent/fees must be positive
  • Right-to-rent status must be verified before tenancy becomes live
  • Guarantor verification must be completed (if present)
  • Break clauses must have valid break dates
  • Tenancy progression through stages (activation → completion → commencement)
  • Renewal options documented and tracked
  • Soft-delete with versioning for audit trail
  • May link to activity (which activity produced this tenancy) and requirement (which requirement was matched)

docs.title: Data Persistence
docs.text:

  • Reference data (Activity Types, Statuses, Party Roles, etc.)

Search/Indexing: Elasticsearch

  • Full-text search on contacts, activities, requirements, properties
  • Aggregations for dashboards and reporting
  • Projection of authoritative SQL data

Blob Storage: Azure Storage

  • Attachments (documents, images, brochures)
  • PDFs, reports
  • Marketing materials

Message Queue: Azure Storage Queue, Service Bus

  • Activity state change events
  • Requirement match notifications
  • Tenancy progression events
  • External integration messages (Fixflo, SAP, etc.)

docs.title: Hub Entity State Machines & Validation Rules
Overview
docs.text: This document details the state machines and validation rules that govern the behavior of Hub's core entities. Each entity follows a strict state progression model, with validations enforcing business rules at every transition.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Activities represent marketing instructions for properties (Sales, Lettings, Purchases, etc.). They progress through a linear lifecycle from creation to completion.

docs.title: State Diagram
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    create["Create Activity"] --> draft["DRAFT"]
    draft -->|Publish / Market| live["LIVE"]
    live -->|Offer Received| underOffer["UNDER_OFFER"]
    underOffer -->|Exchange of Contract| completion["COMPLETION"]
    completion -->|Complete Property Transfer| completed["COMPLETED"]
    underOffer -->|Renegotiate| live
    draft -.->|Authorized withdrawal| withdrawn["WITHDRAWN"]
    live -.->|Authorized withdrawal| withdrawn
    underOffer -.->|Authorized withdrawal| withdrawn
    completion -.->|Authorized withdrawal| withdrawn

docs.title: Valid State Transitions
docs.text: From To Trigger Preconditions Actions DRAFT LIVE Publish • Activity has property assigned• All mandatory details set (address, activity type)• Marketing terms defined Generate marketing content, notify agents LIVE UNDER_OFFER Offer Received • At least one valid offer received• Offer approved by vendor/landlord• No active competing offers requiring priority Update activity status, trigger CDD if applicable LIVE WITHDRAWN Withdraw Instruction • Withdrawal authorized by vendor/landlord• No pending completion Notify all parties, archive offers, delist property LIVE EXPIRED Expiry Date Reached • Current date = Expiry date• Activity marked for auto-expiry Archive activity, notify parties UNDER_OFFER COMPLETION Exchange of Contract • Contract exchanged (documented)• CDD completed (if applicable)• All party conditions satisfied• Survey and finance satisfactory Lock down terms, set completion date UNDER_OFFER LIVE Renegotiate • Offer withdrawn or fell through• Authorized by all parties Reset to LIVE, re-market property UNDER_OFFER WITHDRAWN Withdraw • Both parties agree OR vendor/landlord initiates Terminate offer, archive activity COMPLETION COMPLETED Complete Property Transfer • Completion date reached• All funds transferred• Legal ownership transferred Generate completion statement, trigger integrations COMPLETION WITHDRAWN Complete Withdrawal • Transaction fell through at completion stage Reverse state changes, re-market or archive (Any) WITHDRAWN Force Withdrawal • Authorized withdrawal• Reason documented Notify all parties, cleanup offers/matches

docs.title: Activity Status Validation Rules (Gherkin)
docs.text:
Feature: Activity Status Transitions

  Scenario: Activity cannot go from LIVE to COMPLETED directly
    Given an Activity in LIVE status
    When I attempt to set Activity status to COMPLETED
    Then the operation fails with ValidationException
    And the error message is "Activity must be UNDER_OFFER or COMPLETION before COMPLETED"

  Scenario: Activity cannot transition WITHDRAWN to any other state
    Given an Activity in WITHDRAWN status
    When I attempt to transition it to LIVE
    Then the operation fails with InvalidStateException
    And the error message is "WITHDRAWN is a terminal state"

  Scenario: Offer acceptance automatically moves Activity to UNDER_OFFER
    Given an Activity in LIVE status with multiple offers
    When I accept an offer from the vendor
    Then the Activity status changes to UNDER_OFFER
    And the accepted offer is marked as "Active"
    And all other offers are marked as "Withdrawn" or "Superseded"

  Scenario: Activity expiry must respect the agreed expiry date
    Given an Activity with expiryDate = "2026-12-31"
    When the system date becomes "2027-01-01"
    Then the Activity is automatically moved to EXPIRED status
    And the Activity cannot be re-activated without explicit renewal

  Scenario: Cannot move to COMPLETION without CDD verification (for high-value activities)
    Given an Activity for a property valued >£500,000
    When I attempt to move Activity to COMPLETION
    And CDD verification is not complete
    Then the operation fails with ComplianceException
    And the error message is "CDD must be completed before COMPLETION for activities >£500k"

  Scenario: Multiple properties in a chain must complete together
    Given Activity A (Seller selling) linked to Activity B (Seller buying) in a chain
    When I attempt to complete Activity A before Activity B
    Then the operation fails with ChainTransactionException
    And the error message is "Chain partner activities must complete in order"

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Requirements represent what buyers, tenants, landlords seek. They progress through matching and completion.

docs.title: State Diagram
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    create["Create Requirement"] --> active["ACTIVE"]
    active -->|Match to Activity| matched["MATCHED"]
    matched -->|Offer Accepted / Deal Agreed| completing["COMPLETING"]
    completing -->|Completion Done| completed["COMPLETED"]
    matched -->|Renegotiate| active
    active -.->|Withdraw or expiry| withdrawn["WITHDRAWN / EXPIRED"]
    matched -.->|Withdraw or expiry| withdrawn
    completing -.->|Expiry| expired["EXPIRED"]

docs.title: Valid State Transitions
docs.text: From To Trigger Preconditions Actions ACTIVE MATCHED Match Found • At least one Activity matches criteria• Match score meets threshold (default: >0.7)• Auto-matcher has run OR manual match approved Create Match record, notify applicant ACTIVE EXPIRED Expiry Date Reached • Current date = Requirement expiry date Archive requirement, notify applicant ACTIVE WITHDRAWN Withdraw Requirement • Authorized by applicant• No active offers Archive requirement MATCHED COMPLETING Offer Accepted • Offer accepted from matched Activity• All party conditions met Lock requirement to accepted property MATCHED ACTIVE Renegotiate • No active offer OR applicant requests renegotiation• Previously matched activities still available Reset to ACTIVE for further matching MATCHED WITHDRAWN Withdraw • Applicant decides not to proceed• All offers withdrawn Archive requirement COMPLETING COMPLETED Completion • Activity has completed• All transfer documentation done Mark requirement fulfilled, archive (Any) EXPIRED Manual Expiry • Requirement criteria no longer relevant• User-initiated Archive requirement

docs.title: Requirement Matching Logic
docs.text:
Feature: Requirement Matching

  Scenario: Auto-matcher finds matching activities nightly
    Given a Requirement for Tenant with:
      | propertyType | "Office"           |
      | minSize      | 5000 sqm           |
      | maxSize      | 15000 sqm          |
      | minRent      | £30,000 p/a        |
      | maxRent      | £60,000 p/a        |
      | location     | "London"           |

    And Activities exist:
      | Activity | Type    | Size  | Rent      | Location | Status |
      | ACT-001  | Lettings| 10000 | £45,000   | London   | LIVE   |
      | ACT-002  | Lettings| 3000  | £50,000   | London   | LIVE   |
      | ACT-003  | Lettings| 8000  | £35,000   | Paris    | LIVE   |

    When the nightly matcher runs
    Then only ACT-001 is matched to the Requirement
    And ACT-002 is not matched (size < 5000)
    And ACT-003 is not matched (location ≠ London)

  Scenario: Requirement matching respects activity status
    Given a Requirement matching criteria to multiple Activities
    When some Activities are in WITHDRAWN or COMPLETED status
    Then those Activities are excluded from matching
    And only LIVE and UNDER_OFFER Activities are considered

  Scenario: Matching score reflects how well Activity meets Requirement
    Given a Requirement with strict criteria:
      | propertyType | "Office" (strict)          |
      | size         | 10000 sqm (±10% tolerance) |
      | rent         | £50k (±5% tolerance)       |

    And Activity with:
      | propertyType | "Office" (exact match)     |
      | size         | 10000 sqm (exact match)    |
      | rent         | £50k (exact match)         |

    Then the match score is highest (e.g., 0.99)

    And when Activity has:
      | propertyType | "Office"      |
      | size         | 11000 sqm     | (outside tolerance)
      | rent         | £52k          | (outside tolerance)

    Then the match score is lower (e.g., 0.65)

  Scenario: Once-matched requirement can be matched to multiple activities
    Given a Requirement in MATCHED status matched to Activity-A
    When a new better Activity-B is published that matches the Requirement
    Then the Requirement can receive a second Match notification
    But the applicant must actively accept both or choose one

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Tenancies represent active leases between tenant and landlord. They progress from creation through commencement, renewal, and expiry.

docs.title: State Diagram
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    create["Create Tenancy"] --> draft["DRAFT (pre-activation)"]
    draft -->|Right-to-Rent Check| check["Right-to-Rent verified"]
    check -->|Activate on Commencement Date| active["ACTIVE / LIVE"]
    active -->|Renewal Option Date| renewing["RENEWING"]
    renewing -->|Renewal Rejected| active
    renewing -->|Renewal Agreed| newTenancy["Create New Tenancy"]
    newTenancy --> active
    active -->|Expiry Date Reached| expired["EXPIRED"]
    active -.->|Surrender Agreed| surrendered["SURRENDERED"]
    active -.->|Force Termination| terminated["TERMINATED"]

docs.title: Valid State Transitions
docs.text: From To Trigger Preconditions Actions DRAFT ACTIVE Activate • Right-to-rent verified (if applicable)• All party information complete• Commencement date reached• Rent collection method configured Activate lease, begin rent tracking ACTIVE RENEWING Initiate Renewal • 6 months before expiry date• Renewal option available• Notice given to other party Create renewal proposal, notify parties ACTIVE SURRENDERED Surrender Agreed • Both parties (tenant + landlord) agree• Early termination authorized• Any break conditions met Terminate lease early, vacate property ACTIVE TERMINATED Force Termination • Legal grounds exist (breach, forfeiture)• Proper notice given (per lease terms)• Authorized by landlord/legal Initiate eviction if needed, vacate property RENEWING ACTIVE Renewal Rejected • Either party rejects renewal• No renewal agreement reached Revert to ACTIVE for final months, plan exit RENEWING ACTIVE Renewal Accepted • Both parties agree new terms• New Tenancy created for renewal period Create new Tenancy record, old Tenancy expires ACTIVE EXPIRED Expiry Date Reached • Current date = Expiry date• No renewal agreed Archive tenancy, record as naturally ended (Any) CANCELLED Cancel Pre-Activation • Tenancy in DRAFT status• Before activation• Authorized cancellation Discard tenancy, notify parties

docs.title: Tenancy Activation Preconditions
docs.text:
Feature: Tenancy Activation

  Scenario: Right-to-rent must be verified before activation
    Given a Tenancy in DRAFT status created with:
      | tenantType       | "Company"                    |
      | tenantContactId  | contact-company-001          |

    When I attempt to activate the Tenancy
    And rightToRentVerified = false
    Then the activation fails with ComplianceException
    And the error message is "Right-to-rent verification required for company tenants"

  Scenario: Commencement date must equal or exceed today
    Given a Tenancy in DRAFT status with commencementDate = "2026-01-01"
    When the system date is "2026-12-31" (after commencement)
    Then I cannot activate the Tenancy
    And the error message is "Cannot activate a Tenancy after its commencement date"

  Scenario: Rent collection method must be configured
    Given a Tenancy in DRAFT status
    When I attempt to activate without setting rentPaymentMethod
    Then the activation fails with ValidationException
    And the error message is "Rent collection method (Direct Debit, Standing Order, etc.) must be configured"

  Scenario: Break clause verification for mid-term exits
    Given a Tenancy with breakClause = { breakDate: "2028-01-15" }
    When a Surrender request is submitted after breakDate
    Then the break conditions are waived
    But if surrendered before breakDate
    Then break penalties may apply (per lease terms)

  Scenario: Automatic activation on commencement date
    Given a Tenancy in DRAFT status with commencementDate = "2026-12-25"
    When the system date becomes "2026-12-25"
    Then the Tenancy is automatically activated
    And the status changes from DRAFT to ACTIVE

docs.title: Tenancy Renewal Logic
docs.text:
Feature: Tenancy Renewal

  Scenario: Renewal option opens 6 months before expiry
    Given a Tenancy expiring on "2027-06-30"
    When the system date becomes "2026-12-30" (6 months before)
    Then the Tenancy is flagged as "Available for Renewal"
    And a renewal workflow is initiated

  Scenario: Renewal terms must be agreed by both parties
    Given a Tenancy in RENEWING status
    When the landlord proposes renewal terms:
      | newExpiryDate  | "2030-06-30"           |
      | proposedRent   | £50,000 p/a (+2.2%)    |

    When the tenant accepts the terms:
    Then a new Tenancy record is created with:
      | previousTenancyId | original tenancy ID    |
      | commencementDate  | expiry date + 1 day    |
      | expiryDate        | "2030-06-30"           |
      | rentPerAnnum      | £50,000                |

    And the original Tenancy is closed/archived

  Scenario: If renewal not agreed by expiry date, tenancy expires
    Given a Tenancy in RENEWING status with expiryDate = "2027-06-30"
    When the system date becomes "2027-07-01"
    And no renewal agreement has been reached
    Then the Tenancy moves to EXPIRED status
    And the property becomes available for new letting

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Offers represent an interested party's proposal to purchase/rent a property or proceed with an activity.

docs.title: State Diagram
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    create["Create Offer"] --> pending["PENDING_REVIEW / PENDING"]
    pending -->|Vendor / landlord accepts| accepted["ACCEPTED"]
    pending -->|Vendor / landlord rejects| rejected["REJECTED"]
    pending -->|Offeror withdraws| withdrawn["WITHDRAWN"]

docs.title: Valid State Transitions
docs.text: From To Trigger Preconditions Actions PENDING ACCEPTED Vendor/Landlord Accepts • Valid offer received• Authorized by vendor/landlord• Within expiry window Mark offer as accepted, trigger Activity → UNDER_OFFER PENDING REJECTED Vendor/Landlord Rejects • Offer withdrawn or below asking price• Authorized rejection Mark offer as rejected, notify offeror PENDING WITHDRAWN Offeror Withdraws • Offeror changes mind before acceptance• Withdrawal authorized Mark offer withdrawn, Activity remains LIVE ACTIVE EXPIRED Offer Expiry Date Passes • Current date > expiry date• No action taken Mark offer expired, Activity may remain UNDER_OFFER (if another active offer) ACTIVE WITHDRAWN Later Withdrawal • Offeror withdraws after acceptance• Activity has not yet completed Revert Activity to LIVE if no other active offers

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Contacts are the foundation of Hub data. They must meet strict validation requirements.

docs.title: Contact Types and Required Fields
docs.text:
Feature: Contact Validation

  Scenario: Individual Contact requires minimum information
    Given a Contact with contactType = "Individual"
    When I save the Contact
    Then the following fields are required:
      | firstName    | String, 1-50 chars      |
      | lastName     | String, 1-50 chars      |
      | emailAddress | Valid email format      |

    And optional fields include:
      | middleNames  | String, optional        |
      | dateOfBirth  | Date, optional          |
      | phone        | Phone number, optional  |

  Scenario: Company Contact requires business information
    Given a Contact with contactType = "Company"
    When I save the Contact
    Then the following fields are required:
      | companyName  | String, 1-100 chars     |
      | crn          | UK Company Registration Number (required for UK) |
      | registeredAddress | Full address        |

    And optional fields include:
      | companyPhone | Phone number            |
      | vatNumber    | VAT registration number |
      | directors    | List of director contacts |

  Scenario: Contact must have at least one address
    Given a Contact without any addresses
    When I save the Contact
    Then the operation fails with ValidationException
    And the error message is "Contact must have at least one address"

  Scenario: Contact must have at least one phone or email
    Given a Contact with:
      | phones       | empty list              |
      | emails       | empty list              |

    When I save the Contact
    Then the operation fails with ValidationException
    And the error message is "Contact must have at least one email or phone number"

  Scenario: Email consent rules enforce opt-in/opt-out status
    Given a Contact with email = "buyer@example.com"
    When an email is sent to the Contact
    And the Contact has consentStatus = "OPTED_OUT"
    Then the email send operation fails
    And the error message is "Contact has opted out of email marketing"

  Scenario: Duplicate Contact detection
    Given Contact A with:
      | firstName  | "John"               |
      | lastName   | "Smith"              |
      | email      | "john@example.com"   |

    When I create Contact B with identical details
    Then the system detects a potential duplicate
    And suggests merging or discarding Contact B

  Scenario: Contact merge combines records
    Given Contact A and Contact B identified as duplicates
    When I approve Contact merge (A absorbs B)
    Then:
      | Contact A gets Contact B's addresses   |
      | Contact A gets Contact B's phone numbers |
      | Contact A gets Contact B's linked activities |
      | Contact B is marked as MERGED/ARCHIVED |
      | All activities linked to B now link to A |

docs.title: Negotiator Assignment
docs.text:
Feature: Negotiator Assignment

  Scenario: Every Contact must have a primary Negotiator (assigned staff)
    Given a Contact without a Negotiator assigned
    When I save the Contact
    Then the operation fails with ValidationException
    And the error message is "Contact must have a primary Negotiator"

  Scenario: Negotiator must be active/enabled in the system
    Given a Contact with assignedNegotiator = negotiator-inactive
    When I save the Contact
    Then the operation fails with ValidationException
    And the error message is "Assigned Negotiator is inactive; select an active Negotiator"

  Scenario: Negotiator can be changed during Contact lifecycle
    Given a Contact with assignedNegotiator = negotiator-A
    When I change assignedNegotiator = negotiator-B
    Then all future activities created will assign negotiator-B
    But existing activities linked to negotiator-A remain unchanged

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Properties represent physical real estate assets with strict data requirements.

docs.title: Property Structure
docs.text:
Feature: Property Creation and Validation

  Scenario: Property requires complete address information
    Given a Property without a complete address
    When I save the Property
    Then the operation fails with ValidationException
    And the error message is "Property must have complete address (street, town, postcode)"

  Scenario: Property must have at least one Ownership record
    Given a Property without any Ownership records
    When I save the Property
    Then the operation fails with ValidationException
    And the error message is "Property must have at least one Ownership record"

  Scenario: Ownership percentages must total 100% (or be flexible for fractional ownership)
    Given a Property with Ownerships:
      | Contact | Percentage |
      | Owner-A | 60%        |
      | Owner-B | 30%        |

    When I save the Property
    Then the operation fails (if system enforces 100% rule)
    And the error message is "Ownership percentages must total 100%"

  Scenario: Property characteristics vary by type
    Given a Property with propertyType = "Office"
    When I save the Property
    Then the following characteristics should be provided:
      | totalArea      | Numeric, sqm            |
      | floors         | Integer, number of floors |
      | openPlan       | Boolean                 |
      | meetingRooms   | Integer count           |

  Scenario: Property can have multiple Tenancies simultaneously (multi-let)
    Given a Property with 5 Units
    When I create Tenancies for Units 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
    Then all 5 Tenancies are active simultaneously
    And the Property occupancy = 100% (5/5 units occupied)
    And each unit can track separate rent, parties, and renewal dates
